entries.name: 1Password
entries.definition: A commercial password manager that stores logins and other secrets in encrypted vaults.

entries.name: 360 campaigns
entries.definition: Planning marketing campaigns that carry one message across many channels, such as TV, digital, print and in-store.

entries.name: 3D modeling software
entries.definition: Software used to build three-dimensional models of objects or scenes, for example for design, animation or games.

entries.name: 3D solid and surface modeling
entries.definition: Building three-dimensional models of objects as solids and as surfaces in CAD software.

entries.name: 3D Touch
entries.definition: A pressure-sensitive touchscreen feature on some Apple iPhones that responds differently to light and firm presses.

entries.name: 3DMark
entries.definition: A benchmark program that measures the graphics and processing performance of computers.

entries.name: 4D modeling (construction)
entries.definition: Linking a three-dimensional building model to the construction schedule so the building work can be viewed step by step over time.

entries.name: 50% tissue culture infectious dose (TCID50)
entries.definition: The amount of virus that infects half of the inoculated cell cultures, used as a unit to measure virus infectivity in the laboratory.

entries.name: ABC JavaScript Renderer
entries.definition: A JavaScript library that draws music written in ABC notation as sheet music in a web page.

entries.name: ABEC scale
entries.definition: A rating scale from the Annular Bearing Engineers' Committee that grades the manufacturing tolerances of precision ball bearings.

entries.name: Academic English
entries.definition: The register of English used for scholarly reading, writing and speaking, such as essays and research papers.

entries.name: Academic record-keeping
entries.definition: Maintaining accurate student records such as enrolment, grades and transcripts for a school or university.

entries.name: Accelerated failure time models
entries.definition: A class of survival-analysis regression models in which the covariates act multiplicatively on the time until an event occurs.

entries.name: Accelerated Mobile Pages
entries.definition: An open-source HTML framework, started by Google, for building web pages that load quickly on mobile devices.

entries.name: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy
entries.definition: A form of psychotherapy that helps people accept difficult thoughts and feelings and commit to actions that fit their values.

entries.name: Access point name
entries.definition: The name of a gateway between a mobile network and another network such as the internet, which a device uses to set up a data connection.

entries.name: Accessioning
entries.definition: Formally logging a received specimen or item and giving it a unique identifying number.

entries.name: Accountancy and Passenger Ticket Issuing System
entries.definition: A computerised system for issuing passenger tickets and accounting for the sales.
variants: Accountancy And Passenger Ticket Issuing System (APTIS)

entries.name: Accounting cycle
entries.definition: The sequence of steps an accountant follows from recording a business's transactions to preparing financial statements and closing the books.

entries.name: Accounting software
entries.definition: Software for recording financial transactions and producing ledgers, invoices and financial reports.

entries.name: Accounts receivable management
entries.definition: Tracking invoices and collecting the money that customers owe a business.

entries.name: Accumulated benefit obligation
entries.definition: The present value of pension benefits earned to date, measured on current pay levels without assuming future pay rises.

entries.name: ACID Pro
entries.definition: A loop-based music-making software line first released by Sonic Foundry and later owned by Sony and then Magix.

entries.name: ACL Analytics
entries.definition: Data analysis software that auditors and finance teams use to test large data sets, scripted with a command language called ACLScript.

entries.name: Action for Climate Empowerment
entries.definition: The UN climate process's term for work on climate education, training, public awareness, public participation and access to information.

entries.name: Activated sludge
entries.definition: A wastewater treatment process in which air and a mixed community of microorganisms break down the organic matter in sewage.

entries.name: Active-HDL
entries.definition: An integrated design and simulation environment from Aldec for FPGA and digital-logic designs written in hardware description languages such as VHDL and Verilog.

entries.name: Active pharmaceutical ingredient
entries.definition: The component of a medicine that produces its intended therapeutic effect.

entries.name: ActivePivot
entries.definition: An in-memory analytics engine from ActiveViam for real-time aggregation and multidimensional analysis of large data sets.

entries.name: ActivePython
entries.definition: A commercially supported distribution of the Python programming language from ActiveState.

entries.name: Activities of daily living
entries.definition: The basic self-care tasks of everyday life, such as bathing, dressing, eating and moving about, that carers help with and clinicians use to assess independence.

entries.name: Actuarial exams
entries.definition: The series of professional examinations set by actuarial societies such as the Society of Actuaries and the Casualty Actuarial Society, which candidates pass on the way to actuarial credentials.

entries.name: Acunetix
entries.definition: A web application security scanner that tests websites for vulnerabilities such as SQL injection and cross-site scripting.

entries.name: AD Model Builder
entries.definition: Open-source software for fitting complex nonlinear statistical models using automatic differentiation.

entries.name: AdaBoost
entries.definition: A machine-learning algorithm that combines many weak classifiers into one strong classifier by reweighting the training examples at each round.

entries.name: Adaptive equipment
entries.definition: Devices and tools designed or modified to help people with disabilities or injuries do everyday tasks.

entries.name: Adaptive Insights
entries.definition: Cloud-based business planning, budgeting and forecasting software that Workday acquired in 2018.

entries.name: Adaptive leadership
entries.definition: A leadership approach, developed from the work of Ronald Heifetz and Marty Linsky, that focuses on helping groups adapt to difficult challenges.

entries.name: ADDIE model
entries.definition: An instructional design process with five phases: analysis, design, development, implementation and evaluation.

entries.name: Additive manufacturing
entries.definition: Making physical objects by adding material layer by layer from a digital model, as in 3D printing.
